topics.title: Underperformance
questions: What observable facts show the gap?
Was the standard clearly understood?
Is the main factor skill, clarity, capacity, motivation, process, or context?
topics.framework: Describe the specific situation and behavior, explain impact, invite the employee's perspective, clarify the required standard, agree on support and a review date.
actions: Agree on one measurable improvement and follow-up date

topics.title: Chronic lateness
questions: What pattern and impact can be documented?
Was the schedule expectation explicit?
Is there a barrier the employee wants to discuss through the appropriate process?
topics.framework: Address the pattern promptly and privately. Focus on attendance behavior and operational impact, invite perspective, restate the standard, and follow organizational policy.
actions: Agree on next steps and review consistently

topics.title: Employee coaching
questions: What outcome does the employee want?
What capability would create the greatest impact?
What options has the employee considered?
topics.framework: Coach through questions before advice. Help the employee define the goal, examine current reality, generate options, and choose a commitment.

topics.title: Difficult conversations
questions: What is the shared outcome?
Which facts can be observed directly?
What response are you prepared to hear?
topics.framework: Open with purpose, describe observations without labels, explain impact, ask for perspective, clarify expectations, and close with an agreement.

topics.title: Healthcare leadership
questions: What patient, workforce, quality, or operational outcome is involved?
Which professional roles and expertise must be included?
What safety concern requires escalation?
topics.framework: Use interprofessional role clarity, respectful communication, shared goals, situation awareness, mutual support, and organizational safety processes.
actions: Escalate safety or clinical issues through qualified channels

topics.title: Higher education leadership
questions: What decision rights or governance process applies?
Whose voice and expertise are needed?
How does the issue connect to mission and student success?
topics.framework: Distinguish consultation, recommendation, and decision authority. Build process credibility through transparency, stakeholder inclusion, and clear follow-through.
actions: Explain how input shaped the decision

topics.title: Family enterprise leadership
questions: Is this a family, ownership, or management issue?
Who has decision authority?
What transition or governance mechanism is needed?
topics.framework: Separate family, ownership, and business roles. Clarify forums, decision rights, standards, and transition milestones while preserving relationships and enterprise continuity.
actions: Name the role each person is speaking from
Move the issue to the correct forum

topics.title: 360 leadership feedback
questions: Which behavior should raters observe?
What examples support the rating?
What strength and development priority emerge?
topics.framework: Use observable behaviors across Leading Self, Relationships, Teams, Performance, Change, and the System. Avoid personality labels.
